transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Wells (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Daniel Hart (Pinegrove Head of Platform), Leila Ortiz (Security Engineer), Marcus Yu (DevOps)
Shared artifacts: Redwood SOC2 summary (link), ISO scope doc (link), sample SAML config (link), demo deck: /decks/pinegrove-intake.pdf

Summary:
Pinegrove is evaluating Redwood for inference powering grid forecasts and outage prediction models. Primary concerns: encryption at rest/in-transit, KMS/HSM integration, SSO/SAML + RBAC mapping, audit logs and retention windows, and data residency for EU clients. They want to understand tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for compliance and cost.

Topics covered:
- SOC2/ISO posture and artifact availability
- SSO/SAML integration pattern and IdP mapping to RBAC
- Encryption key management (KMS, customer-managed keys, HSM)
- Audit logs, retention policy, exportability
- Deployment options for regulated workloads (VPC, on-prem)
- Performance/latency implications of Dedicated vs Hosted

Action items (recap at end duplicated in metadata)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. i'm Jordan with Redwood — i'm joined by priya our solutions engineer. quick roll call?
[00:12] Daniel: yes daniel here. we have leila and marcus on, thanks.
[00:18] Priya: great, i can do the security heavy lift here. quick agenda: run through compliance posture, keys and kms options, sso and rbac, then discuss deployment choices and next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Leila: yep that's perfect. we have a pretty strict scope — SOC2 type II is table stakes, ISO is optional but preferred. also we need customer-managed keys ideally.
[00:39] Marcus: and to add, we operate in aws primarily, some eu data centers for customers in frankfurt, so data residency matters.
[00:48] Jordan: understood. to start: redwood is SOC2 Type II — we can share the report and a redacted scope doc, and we also have an ISO27001 certificate in scope for certain regions, i'll send the scoping doc after.
[01:05] Leila: when you say "send the report" — is that full artifact or a summary? also we need to know control mapping to our internal framework for procurement.
[01:15] Jordan: we typically share the attestation and a SOC2 summary plus a control map on an NDA. full workpapers aren't provided but we do provide enough to satisfy vendor risk — we'll attach the control mappings.
[01:28] Leila: ok that's workable. on to keys — what's your KMS model for hosted? customer-managed CMKs? do you support external HSMs?
[01:39] Priya: good question. hosted mode supports CMKs via AWS KMS with customer-managed keys — you can bring your own key in an AWS account we either integrate via cross-account key policy or use a customer KMS gateway. for Dedicated and Private we support KMS integration and optional on-prem HSM via external KMS (PKCS#11 integration) — though the latter requires network peering and some setup.
[02:06] Marcus: does that mean in hosted you'd need cross-account role? how does it affect latency when decrypting model artifacts or on token-level encryption?
[02:15] Priya: the key ops for model load are async — decryption happens at container startup. per-request encryption for payloads is TLS in transit and envelope encryption using the CMK for stored artifacts. per-token operations don't hit KMS inline. latency impact for inference is negligible.
[02:30] Daniel: we need to be sure keys are rotatable and that audit trails show who rotated and when — that is a gating control for us.
[02:38] Priya: yes, rotation for CMKs is supported and audit logs include KMS operations surfaced in Redwood audit logs and we can ingest cloudtrail or forward them to your SIEM.
[02:48] Leila: speaking of audit logs — retention windows? our policy is 7 years for certain auth events, 1 year for others. can your system retain at that granularity?
[02:59] Jordan: short answer: yes, with caveats. Hosted defaults to 90 days for interactive logs but we offer extended log retention as an add-on or via forwarding to customer's S3/SIEM for long-term retention. Dedicated/Private gives you full control — you can set retention to your policy and keep logs in your environment.
[03:16] Leila: so for hosted, to meet 7 years we'd need to forward logs to our S3 or Splunk?
[03:22] Priya: exactly. we can stream audit events in real-time to a customer-owned bucket or syslog endpoint. we also provide a redwood-managed archival option but for long-retention enterprise customers prefer their own storage.
[03:34] Daniel: what about SSO / SAML? we use Okta and expect SCIM + SAML and group mapping to roles.
[03:42] Priya: we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0. typical pattern: IdP asserts group membership, we map groups to Redwood roles (admin, developer, readonly) through RBAC policies. we can provide sample mappings and metadata to import into Okta.
[03:56] Marcus: any gotchas with multiple IdPs or multi-tenant setups? we have partners connecting via separate identity providers.
[04:04] Priya: we support multiple identity providers per account and can map them to separate RBAC scopes. there's some manual config for mapping external groups to internal roles but it's supported.
[04:15] Leila: we need fine-grained RBAC — ideally ability to limit model access by team and to restrict certain sensitive models to a smaller group.
[04:24] Jordan: yep, RBAC is per-route and per-model — you can create policies that limit who can call a particular model or who can deploy. we'll send examples.
[04:33] Leila: auditability: can we export a timeline of who accessed which model and prompt payloads? we can't store PII in logs by default.
[04:42] Priya: we log model calls with metadata and a unique request id. by default payloads are not stored beyond the configured retention, and we mask PII via configurable scrubbing rules. For hosted, you can choose to enable full request logging delivered to your S3. Dedicated/Private keep everything in your VPC.
[04:58] Daniel: curious about data residency — if a user in EU hits the hosted endpoint, will data pass through US infra?
[05:06] Jordan: routing is region aware. hosted endpoints default to the region you choose; we have EU regions so data stays in region for those requests. for strict residency customers we recommend Dedicated or Private so traffic never leaves your network.
[05:20] Marcus: we heard about model fallbacks and routing policies — if capacity in eu is constrained does the system route to us-west as fallback? that's a no-go for us.
[05:30] Priya: you can configure hard region policies that disallow cross-region fallback. default may allow fallback for high availability, but for customers with residency requirements we enforce strict region pinning.
[05:42] Leila: encryption in transit — you mentioned TLS; do you support mTLS for intra-service calls and customer authentication?
[05:50] Priya: yes, internal service-to-service can be mTLS; as for customer-facing, we support mutual TLS for dedicated/private connections and client cert auth for certain enterprise integrations.
[06:01] Daniel: let's talk procurement: we need evidence of pen test, vulnerability scanning cadence, and service-level agreements.
[06:09] Jordan: we run quarterly vuln scans and annual pentests, and we can provide an executive summary and scan cadence. SLA is available for Dedicated contracts — hosted has standard uptime commitments and we can negotiate enterprise SLAs on committed capacity.
[06:23] Leila: is there support for bringing our own audit agent into the runtime? we run an EDR and need visibility.
[06:30] Priya: on Dedicated/Private you can install or forward agents; hosted is more limited but we can integrate with trace exporters and forward logs to your observability stack.
[06:40] Marcus: can we schedule a short benchmark to see latency differences? the tradeoff between Dedicated (lower latency) and hosted cost is a key decision point.
[06:48] Jordan: absolutely — Priya can provision a small dedicated pool for a two-week trial and run your model against typical load. we'll include cost estimates and token/unit usage metrics.
[06:59] Leila: one more on legal/regulatory: do you support data subject requests and data deletion workflows? we need ability to delete datasets and associated logs on demand.
[07:08] Priya: yes — we have deletion APIs and documented workflows, but hosted deletion has typical caveats around backups and retention windows; Dedicated/Private gives you stronger guarantees since storage is in your control.
[07:22] Daniel: good. any integrations with our KMS provider besides AWS — we use HashiCorp Vault for certain keys.
[07:29] Priya: we have integrations with Vault via transit and can call external KMS endpoints; again this is most straightforward in Dedicated/Private where network reachability is simpler.
[07:40] Jordan: quick note on pricing — long retention and log forwarding are billable add-ons. Dedicated is more predictable but higher baseline; hosted is lower entry cost. we'll follow up with a pricing spreadsheet.
[07:54] Leila: any compliance blockers you foresee for energy sector? we're subject to NERC CIP for some systems.
[08:02] Priya: Redwood isn't currently certified to NERC CIP specifically; for systems under that scope we typically recommend Private/on-prem deployments where customers control the entire stack. we can discuss a gap analysis if you want.
[08:15] Marcus: ok that's helpful.
[08:18] Jordan: let me recap: we'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts (Jordan), Priya will send SAML/SCIM metadata and RBAC examples, we'll provision a Dedicated trial cluster for benchmarking, Marcus will provide retention windows and contact list. we'll schedule a follow-up with networking + security next week.
[08:36] Leila: sounds good. any other quick Qs?
[08:39] Marcus: when would the trial start?
[08:42] Priya: we can spin up the trial in 3-5 business days once we have the network/peering and an approved scope.
[08:50] Daniel: perfect. thanks all.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional words garbled ("K V cache" vs "KV cache"), some names slightly off in auto transcripts. crosstalk noted at 04:00 when multiple people chimed in.
